newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-Political analysts comments on UK election.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Political analysts comments on UK election.

text.p: Following is a selection of comments from political analysts on the outcome of Britain's May 1 parliamentary election, made as results were announced.
2110 GMT - MICHAEL THRASHER, PROFESSOR OF POLITICS AT PLYMOUTH UNIVERSITY
(After BBC, ITN, Sky exit polls pointed to overwhelming Labour majority)

"The Conservatives haven't polled this figure since 1832. So this election could be of historic proportions...The latest Gallup regional poll pointed to a majority of over 200 (seats, but) the exit figures are far more reliable. We are now looking around a Labour majority of around 160 to 180 seats."
2118 GMT - COLIN RALLINGS, PROFESSOR OF POLITICS AT PLYMOUTH UNIVERSITY (after MORI exit poll for ITN television news)

"It is in line with the campaign polls. A number of people thought it couldn't happen but if it does, Labour will have its largest majority ever, the Conservatives will have their lowest share of the vote since at least 1859, and their could be the largest third party in parliament since 1923 -- An historic night indeed."
